youtube.title: Why America Built 1,500 Malls Just to Let Them Die
youtube.description:
A 1954 tax rule made it cheaper to build a brand-new mall than to keep an old one full. Most people blame online shopping for America's dead malls, but the real story starts in Congress: accelerated depreciation let owners of new buildings claim huge paper losses in the early years, so it paid to build, sell and build again down the road. Victor Gruen's dream town square became a tax machine, until 1986 pulled the plug. Sources: Hanchett, American Historical Review (1996); Gladwell, The New Yorker (2004). The Hidden Why: the reason behind the things you see every day. #TheHiddenWhy #facts #explained
